1.init: comment t.rotation_band_diff - joint turning by timescale
1.name: comment

2.name: text_block

0.name: block
0.value:
Breaks each joint's movement into timescales: for every joint and every band, how much that joint turned this frame once the turning is smoothed down to that band.

Use it on a whole pose stream to tell slow movement from fast in one step - the swing of an arm and the tremor in it come out as different numbers. One frame in gives [joints, bands, 3] out.

HOW IT WORKS:
Each joint's rotation is turned into a form that can be filtered (the first two rows of its rotation matrix) and passed through a bank of LOWPASS filters, one per band, each cutting off at its band's upper edge. So band 1 keeps everything below about 8 Hz (nearly the raw movement) and the last keeps only the slowest drift. Each filtered copy is turned back into a rotation, and the node reports the rotation from last frame's copy to this frame's, as an axis-angle vector (its length is the angle in radians), multiplied by that band's GAIN. Because the bands are lowpass, a fast tremor shows only in the first bands, while a slow sway shows in all of them.

The gains make the slow bands, which move very little per frame, big enough to see: by default 2.25, 2.25, 3.375, 5.06, 7.59, 11.39, 17.09 from the fastest band to the slowest (1.5 times more per band). Send the message band_gains followed by one number per band to set your own. The band edges follow t.filter_bank's rules: 'number of bands' counts edges, so the default 8 gives 7 bands, highest first; report_bands prints them.

SYNTAX:
t.rotation_band_diff
No arguments.

EXAMPLE:
t.rotation_band_diff

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

rotations:
[joints, 3] axis-angle or [joints, 4] quaternions (w first). A flat list of joints is split by 'input format'. Each arrival is one frame. The first frame (and the first after reset) sends nothing: there is no previous frame to compare with.

reset (button):
Empties the filters and forgets the previous frame. Unlike t.filter_bank's reset it does not pre-fill the filters.

input format (menu: auto, axis-angle, quaternion):
How a FLAT input is split into joints: every 3 or every 4 numbers. auto decides from the length, and gives up (with a console message) when the length divides by both 3 and 4 - set it explicitly for SMPL poses of 72 values.

sample freq (Hz, default 60): the rate frames really arrive at.

number of bands (default 8): band edges, one more than the bands.

low / high (Hz, defaults 0.01 and 8): the range of the band edges.

order (1 to 8, default 1): how steeply each lowpass cuts.

band scaling (log or linear), overlap fraction (default 0): as on t.filter_bank.

Changing a setting rebuilds the bank (and the gains return to default if the number of bands no longer matches them).

OUTPUTS:

banded rotation diffs:
[joints, bands, 3]: per joint and band, this frame's turn as an axis-angle vector, times the band's gain.

READING THE DEMO:
np.linalg.norm (axis 2) turns each vector into its length - how much the joint turned in that band this frame - and heat_scroll draws the 7 bands as 7 rows scrolling left, the fastest band at the top. The jitter and the glitches light up the top rows; the slow turning back and forth glows in every row and fades where the turn reverses; the quick turns flash through all of them.

RELATED:
t.filter_bank is the general band splitter for ordinary values. quaternion_diff_and_axis measures frame-to-frame rotation without bands.
